gen_risks.description: Financial management staff overload at the Directorate General of Administration and Finance may lead to delays in transaction processing and financial reporting.
gen_risks.mitigation: Appoint adequate FM staff, including government officers and consultants, within three months of project signing and implement the updated Financial Management Manual.
gen_risks.evidence: The current FM staff at the Directorate General of Administration and Finance may be overloaded, potentially leading to delays in processing transactions and reporting.

gen_risks.description: Delayed approval of the Annual Work Plan and Budget (AWPB) may impede the timely implementation of project activities.
gen_risks.mitigation: Adopt simplified AWPB templates and standardized submission schedules as specified in the Financial Management Manual.
gen_risks.evidence: The delayed approval of the Annual Work Plan and Budget (AWPB) may hinder the timely implementation of project activities.

gen_risks.description: Decentralized school mentoring funding disbursed directly to primary school clusters may not be properly monitored or audited.
gen_risks.mitigation: Issue formal guidelines on School Mentoring Funding within the Project Operations Manual and perform regular internal audit reviews.
gen_risks.evidence: There is a risk that school mentoring funding, which is to be spent at the schools, may not be properly monitored.

gen_risks.description: MoEYS staff's limited experience with World Bank Procurement Regulations could cause procedural non-compliance and execution delays.
gen_risks.mitigation: Assign dedicated full-time government procurement officers and deliver continuous World Bank procurement and STEP system training.
gen_risks.evidence: MoEYS staff’s limited knowledge and experience with the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations, potentially resulting in project implementation delays and noncompliance

gen_risks.description: Delays in obtaining technical specifications and inputs from implementing departments could bottleneck procurement processing.
gen_risks.mitigation: Designate dedicated focal points in technical departments to coordinate inputs and enforce standard operational timelines in the POM.
gen_risks.evidence: possible delays in receiving technical inputs for procurement

gen_risks.description: Governance vulnerabilities and corrupt practices in procurement could compromise contract integrity and cost-efficiency.
gen_risks.mitigation: Enforce public disclosure of procurement plans and contract awards, implement a procurement complaint mechanism, and track transactions in STEP.
gen_risks.evidence: governance risks, including corrupt practices in procurement

gen_risks.description: Inadequate contract supervision and management capacity among implementing units may result in construction delays and vendor underperformance.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide targeted contract management training to the procurement team and delegate adequate evaluation and oversight authority.
gen_risks.evidence: inadequate capacity for contract supervision and management, which may result in implementation delays

gen_risks.description: Internal clearance delays from the Procurement Review Committee could stall contract approvals and project momentum.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish strict service standards in the Project Operations Manual and grant sufficient delegation of authority to committee members.
gen_risks.evidence: possible delays in internal clearance from procurement review committee.

gen_risks.description: Recurrent floods, tropical cyclones, and extreme heatwaves cause school closures, lost instructional time, and infrastructure damage.
gen_risks.mitigation: Construct elevated, climate-resilient facilities with passive cooling and solar power, and deploy EdTech for remote learning continuity.
gen_risks.evidence: Natural disasters caused by climate change, including floods, cyclones, and extreme heat, pose significant challenges for Cambodia, particularly affecting the continuity of education

gen_risks.description: Transitioning Early Grade Learning from donor-supported pilots to nationwide government delivery risks loss of implementation fidelity.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement an implementation science-informed learning agenda with rapid testing, process evaluations, and cluster core-mentor coaching.
gen_risks.evidence: Transitioning from successful, donor-funded interventions with limited geographic coverage to implementation at scale through government systems requires overcoming the many technical, financial, political economy, and capability constraints

gen_risks.description: Incomplete inter-agency alignment between MoEYS and MCS or failure of Phase 1 feasibility criteria could block progression to Phase 2 HRMIS development.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish a joint MoEYS-MCS working group and enforce strict Phase 1 technical and regulatory review milestones before Phase 2 commitment.
gen_risks.evidence: Progression to Phase 2 is conditional on Phase 1 results demonstrating quality and feasibility in terms of (a) technical and system development

gen_risks.description: Insufficient teacher capacity and poor human resource management severely undermine foundational learning achievement in primary schools.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide structured EGL lesson plans, continuous professional development, cluster coaching, and modernize HRMIS for improved teacher allocation.
gen_risks.evidence: insufficient teacher capacity to effectively fulfill their roles... and poor human resources management, which impedes the efficient utilization of allocated resources.

gen_risks.description: Prevalence of physical and sexual violence in rural contexts poses safety risks to female students and staff in education environments.
gen_risks.mitigation: Conduct GBV awareness training for primary teachers, operationalize an SEA/SH-sensitive grievance redress mechanism, and execute GBV action plans.
gen_risks.evidence: 10 percent of women ages 15–49 have experienced physical violence since the age of 15, and 3 percent have faced sexual violence.

gen_risks.description: Civil works construction for childcare centers, preschools, and primary classrooms may trigger land acquisition or land use restrictions.
gen_risks.mitigation: Apply Environmental and Social Management Framework (ESMF) procedures to verify unencumbered public land prior to initiating civil works.
gen_risks.evidence: ESS 5: Land Acquisition, Restrictions on Land Use and Involuntary Resettlement Relevant

gt_risks.description: Environment and Social risk is rated Substantial due to (a) limited institutional capacity to manage environmental and social risks and impacts; (b) nationwide implementation of the project's activities; (c) possible exclusion of vulnerable groups (such as poor children, children with disabilities, and indigenous groups); and (d) other risks involving child protection, occupational health and safety, labor issues, and sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment (SEA/SH).
gt_risks.mitigation: The project will develop a capacity-building plan for the Environmental and Social Safeguards Office and Project Management Unit, including hiring dedicated environmental and social specialists and providing targeted training. It will establish robust monitoring mechanisms to ensure support for vulnerable groups (universal design in new school/WASH construction, materials adapted for visually impaired students), strict adherence to worker codes of conduct, complaint redress and referral mechanisms, and construction site safety measures to protect school children and communities from labor influx and construction-related risks.
